column4: Show the names of editors that are on the committee of journals with sales bigger than 3000.
column5: SELECT T2.Name FROM journal_committee AS T1 JOIN editor AS T2 ON T1.Editor_ID  =  T2.Editor_ID JOIN journal AS T3 ON T1.Journal_ID  =  T3.Journal_ID WHERE T3.Sales  >  3000

FROM editor e

column4: List the date, theme and sales of the journal which did not have any of the listed editors serving on committee.

SELECT j.Date, j.Theme, j.Sales
FROM journal j

)

column6:
SELECT T1.balance AS checking_balance, T2.balance AS savings_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS AS T1
JOIN CHECKING AS T3 ON T1.custid = T3.custid
JOIN SAVINGS AS T4 ON T1.custid = T4.custid
WHERE T1.name = 'Brown';

column4: What is the name corresponding to the accoung with the lowest sum of checking and savings balances?
column5: SELECT T1.name FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN checking AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid JOIN savings AS T3 ON T1.custid  =  T3.custid ORDER BY T2.balance + T3.balance LIMIT 1
column6:
SELECT T1.name 
FROM ACCOUNTS AS T1 
JOIN (
    SELECT custid, SUM(balance) AS total_balance 
    FROM (CHECKING AS T2 
         JOIN SAVINGS AS T3 ON T2.custid = T3.custid) 
    GROUP BY custid
) AS T4 ON T1.custid = T4.custid 
ORDER BY T4.total_balance ASC 
LIMIT 1;

column4: Find the names and total checking and savings balances of accounts whose savings balance is higher than the average savings balance.
column5: SELECT T1.name ,  T2.balance + T3.balance FROM accounts AS T1 JOIN checking AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid JOIN savings AS T3 ON T1.custid  =  T3.custid WHERE T3.balance  >  (SELECT avg(balance) FROM savings)
column6:
SELECT A.name, SUM(C.balance) AS checking_balance, SUM(S.balance) AS savings_balance
FROM ACCOUNTS A
JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
JOIN SAVINGS S ON A.custid = S.custid
WHERE S.balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM SAVINGS)
GROUP BY A.custid, A.name;

column6:
SELECT A.name, C.balance
FROM ACCOUNTS A
JOIN CHECKING C ON A.custid = C.custid
JOIN (
    SELECT custid, MIN(balance) AS min_savings_balance
    FROM SAVINGS
    GROUP BY custid
) S ON A.custid = S.custid
WHERE C.balance > 0;

FROM SAVINGS S
JOIN (

    FROM CHECKING
    GROUP BY custid
) C ON S.custid = C.custid

column4: Find the total checking and saving balance of all accounts sorted by the total balance in ascending order.
column5: SELECT T1.balance + T2.balance FROM checking AS T1 JOIN savings AS T2 ON T1.custid  =  T2.custid ORDER BY T1.balance + T2.balance
column6:
SELECT 
    a.custid,
    a.name,
    SUM(c.balance) AS checking_balance,
    SUM(s.balance) AS savings_balance,
    SUM(c.balance) + SUM(s.balance) AS total_balance
FROM 
    ACCOUNTS a
LEFT JOIN 
    CHECKING c ON a.custid = c.custid
LEFT JOIN 
    SAVINGS s ON a.custid = s.custid
GROUP BY 
    a.custid, a.name

column4: Find all 200 meter and 300 meter results of swimmers with nationality "Australia".

column4: Find the names of swimmers who has a result of "win".

column4: Find the name and nationality of the swimmer who has won (i.e., has a result of "win") more than 1 time.

FROM swimmer s

column4: Find the names of the swimmers who have both "win" and "loss" results in the record.
column5: SELECT t1.name FROM swimmer AS t1 JOIN record AS t2 ON t1.id  =  t2.swimmer_id WHERE RESULT  =  'Win' INTERSECT SELECT t1.name FROM swimmer AS t1 JOIN record AS t2 ON t1.id  =  t2.swimmer_id WHERE RESULT  =  'Loss'

column4: Find the names of stadiums that some Australian swimmers have been to.

column4: Show the id and builder of the railway that are associated with the most trains.

column4: Show the product name and total order quantity for each product.
column5: SELECT T1.product_name ,  sum(T2.order_quantity) FROM products AS T1 JOIN order_items AS T2 ON T1.product_id  =  T2.product_id GROUP BY T1.product_id
column6:

column4: What are the name and phone of the customer with the most ordered product quantity?
column5: SELECT  T1.customer_name ,  T1.customer_phone FROM customers AS T1 JOIN customer_orders AS T2 ON T1.customer_id  =  T2.customer_id JOIN order_items AS T3 ON T3.order_id  =  T2.order_id GROUP BY T1.customer_id ORDER BY sum(T3.order_quantity) DESC LIMIT 1
column6:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.customer_phone
FROM Customers c
JOIN (
    SELECT oi.customer_id, SUM(oi.order_quantity) AS total_quantity
    FROM Order_Items oi
    GROUP BY oi.customer_id
    ORDER BY total_quantity DESC
    LIMIT 1
) o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

column4: How many students are older than 20 in each dorm?

column4: Which city has the least number of customers whose type code is "Good Credit Rating"?
column5: SELECT town_city FROM customers WHERE customer_type_code  =  "Good Credit Rating" GROUP BY town_city ORDER BY count(*) LIMIT 1

column4: Return the city with the customer type code "Good Credit Rating" that had the fewest customers.
column5: SELECT town_city FROM customers WHERE customer_type_code  =  "Good Credit Rating" GROUP BY town_city ORDER BY count(*) LIMIT 1

column4: Find the emails of customers who has filed a complaints of the product with the most complaints.
column5: SELECT t1.email_address FROM customers AS t1 JOIN complaints AS t2 ON t1.customer_id  =  t2.customer_id GROUP BY t1.customer_id ORDER BY count(*) LIMIT 1
column6:
SELECT DISTINCT c.email_address
FROM Customers c
JOIN Complaints co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
WHERE co.product_id = (
    SELECT p.product_id
    FROM Products p
    JOIN Complaints cp ON p.product_id = cp.product_id
    GROUP BY p.product_id
    ORDER BY COUNT(cp.complaint_id) DESC
    LIMIT 1
)

column4: What are the emails of customers who have filed complaints on the product which has had the greatest number of complaints?

FROM Customers c
JOIN Complaints co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
JOIN Products p ON co.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.product_id = (
    SELECT product_id
    FROM Complaints
    GROUP BY product_id
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
    LIMIT 1
)

column4: Which products has been complained by the customer who has filed least amount of complaints?

ORDER BY COUNT(c.complaint_id) ASC

column4: Return the names of products that have had complaints filed by the customer who has filed the fewest complaints.

column4: Find the last name of the staff member who processed the complaint of the cheapest product.
column5: SELECT t1.last_name FROM staff AS t1 JOIN complaints AS t2 ON t1.staff_id  =  t2.staff_id JOIN products AS t3 ON t2.product_id  =  t3.product_id ORDER BY t3.product_price LIMIT 1

FROM Complaints AS T1
JOIN Products AS T2 ON T1.product_id = T2.product_id
JOIN Staff AS T3 ON T1.staff_id = T3.staff_id
